parts.visual:
A telephone is useless if you are the only person on earth who owns one. But if everyone on earth owns one, it is the most valuable tool in history.

The Phenomenon:
1. Network Effects: A phenomenon whereby a product or service gains additional value as more people use it.
2. The Defense: Once a startup achieves strong Network Effects, it becomes a mathematical monopoly. It is almost impossible for a competitor to steal their users, even with a technically superior product.
parts.audio: Venture Capitalists are obsessed with Network Effects. If your product gets better simply because more people use it, you have discovered the most powerful defensive moat in modern capitalism.

questions.question: A brilliant engineer builds a social network that is 10x faster and visually better than Facebook. They launch it. Nobody uses it. Why did the superior product fail?
options: Network Effects. Facebook's value isn't its code; its value is that all your friends are already there. The new app has zero friends on it, so its value is zero, regardless of the technology.
The code was written in Python.
questions.correct_answer: Network Effects. Facebook's value isn't its code; its value is that all your friends are already there. The new app has zero friends on it, so its value is zero, regardless of the technology.
questions.explanation: You cannot beat a network effect with better software. You can only beat it with a new paradigm.

questions.question: Listen to the Uber executive. What specific type of Network Effect is she describing?
questions.tts_text: More drivers mean shorter wait times for riders. Shorter wait times attract more riders. More riders mean more money for drivers, which attracts even more drivers. The cycle feeds itself.
options: A Two-Sided Network Effect (or Marketplace Effect). The value for Group A (Riders) goes up when the number of people in Group B (Drivers) increases, and vice versa.
questions.correct_answer: A Two-Sided Network Effect (or Marketplace Effect). The value for Group A (Riders) goes up when the number of people in Group B (Drivers) increases, and vice versa.
questions.explanation: This is why Uber and Airbnb are so difficult to compete with.

questions.question: What is the 'Cold Start Problem'?
options: The brutal challenge of launching a Network Effect business. Since the platform has no value when it has zero users, how do you convince the very first users to join?
questions.correct_answer: The brutal challenge of launching a Network Effect business. Since the platform has no value when it has zero users, how do you convince the very first users to join?
questions.explanation: Tinder solved this by throwing massive college parties where you had to download the app to get in.

questions.question: Are 'Viral Growth' and 'Network Effects' the same thing?
options: No. Viral Growth is about *Acquisition* (users inviting users to get free stuff). Network Effects are about *Retention and Value* (the product is actually better because there are more users).
Yes, if it's a mobile app.
questions.correct_answer: No. Viral Growth is about *Acquisition* (users inviting users to get free stuff). Network Effects are about *Retention and Value* (the product is actually better because there are more users).
questions.explanation: A virus can spread fast and die fast. A network is a permanent structure.
